newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Surgical makes offer valuing Circon at $218 million.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Surgical makes offer valuing Circon at $218 million.

text.p: U.S. Surgical Corp. said Tuesday it started another hostile tender offer for Circon Corp., a maker of devices for minimally invasive surgery that it has been pursuing for a year.

The offer, which values Circon at about $218 million, is for $16.50 a share. U.S. Surgical, of Norwalk, Conn., also makes products meant to lower the cost of surgery and other medical treatments. It already owns 14.8 percent of Circon.

U.S. Surgical called the new offer "highly attractive" for Circon shareholders and said that while it would prefer to negotiate a friendly deal with Circon management, "they have turned down every request for a meeting."

U.S. Surgical said its offer was subject to it acquiring at least 67 percent of Circon's shares and on cancelling Circon's "poison pill" antitakeover plan. The offer is to expire on Sept. 25, it said.
U.S. Surgical's stake in Circon is as big as possible without triggering Circon's "poison pill."

U.S. Surgical acquired about 1 million Circon shares on the open market before it started an $18-a-share cash tender offer on Aug. 2, 1996. After amending the original offer twice, it acquired another 973,174 shares in a separate offer completed on July 14, 1997.
U.S. Surgical said that since its original offer made on Aug. 2, 1996, Circon's financial performance has "continuously deteriorated."

U.S. Surgical said it fits well with Circon, which is the biggest producer of laparoscopic scopes, video systems and endoscopic suction irrigation devices, used in surgery and for diagnosis, in the United States.
Circon stock rose 87.5 cents to $15.75 on Nasdaq.
